messages.content: I have the Atlanta addresses now. District office is 3100 Cumberland Boulevard SE. The two restaurants are 2955 Cobb Parkway SE and 3621 Vinings Slope SE. Compare hotels that keep all three drives reasonable.

Those points form a compact triangle around Cumberland and Vinings. I’ll compare properties near the center rather than putting you beside only one restaurant. Before I total them, should I price the requested two-night stay and also show the incremental cost of adding Tuesday night for the Wednesday flight scenario?
Yes. I need the full reimbursable amount, not the headline room rate. Break out parking, and tell me exactly when cancellation closes.

I found three practical options. For the two-night base stay, Courtyard Atlanta Vinings/Galleria is $418.36 complete: $349.00 room, $49.36 estimated taxes, and $20.00 self-parking. Hotel Indigo Atlanta-Vinings is $461.72 complete: $372.00 room, $53.72 taxes, and $36.00 parking. Hampton Inn Atlanta-Cumberland Mall is $389.18 complete: $342.00 room and $47.18 taxes, with self-parking included.
What room types are those? I don’t want a total built on a prepaid or noncancelable rate.

All three are flexible rates. Courtyard is a King Guest Room, Hotel Indigo is a Standard King, and Hampton is a King Study. None requires prepayment, though each may place a card guarantee. The quoted totals include mandatory lodging charges and estimated taxes; refundable incidentals are excluded.
Give me the cancellation deadlines in both Atlanta and Chicago time.

Courtyard can be canceled without penalty through Sunday, February 22 at 11:59 p.m. Atlanta time, which is 10:59 p.m. in Chicago. Hotel Indigo closes at the same local deadline: February 22 at 11:59 p.m. Atlanta, or 10:59 p.m. Chicago. Hampton is more restrictive: Saturday, February 21 at 11:59 p.m. Atlanta, or 10:59 p.m. Chicago. After those deadlines, each can charge one night plus tax.
Now the drives. Use Tuesday morning for the office, then realistic late-morning and afternoon traffic to each restaurant.

From Courtyard, allow about 8-12 minutes to the district office at 8:00 a.m., 7-10 minutes to the Cobb Parkway restaurant late morning, and 5-8 minutes to Vinings Slope in the afternoon. From Hotel Indigo, the estimates are 10-14 minutes to the office, 9-13 minutes to Cobb Parkway, and 2-5 minutes to Vinings Slope. From Hampton, allow 6-10 minutes to the office, 4-7 minutes to Cobb Parkway, and 11-16 minutes to Vinings Slope. These are planning ranges; an incident on I-285 or Cumberland Boulevard can add materially more.
The Indigo does not seem worth the extra money. Drop it unless there is some operational advantage I’m missing.

There is no meaningful operational advantage for this route. It is closest to Vinings Slope, but Courtyard is only a few minutes farther and is better balanced across all three stops. I’ll remove Hotel Indigo from the working comparison.
Price the extra night at the Courtyard and Hampton. I want the actual increase including parking and tax, not the new average nightly rate.

Adding Tuesday night increases Courtyard by $211.84: $174.50 room, $27.34 estimated tax, and $10.00 parking. Its three-night complete total becomes $630.20. Hampton increases by $194.59: $171.00 room and $23.59 estimated tax, with parking still included. Its three-night total becomes $583.77.
How do those hotel differences interact with the two return flights? The Tuesday Delta fare was higher.

Using the carried flight prices, the late-Tuesday return is $271 and the early-Wednesday return is $224, a $47 airfare savings for Wednesday. Against that, the added hotel night is $211.84 at Courtyard or $194.59 at Hampton. Hotel plus airfare therefore favors the Tuesday return by $164.84 at Courtyard and $147.59 at Hampton, before the additional rental-car day, fuel, or parking. The Wednesday flight buys schedule protection, but it does not reduce total trip cost.
For the Tuesday flight, assume I leave the Cumberland area at 5:00 p.m. Does either hotel create a problem if I need to pick up a bag after the last review?

Courtyard is the cleaner choice for that sequence. From the district office, it is roughly 8-12 minutes to the hotel, and the hotel is positioned for a direct run toward ATL afterward. Hampton is slightly closer to the office, but retrieving a bag there can pull you back toward the mall entrances and add several traffic lights. Neither makes the 9:12 p.m. departure unworkable, but Courtyard leaves a somewhat simpler exit.
Can I leave the car at either one after checkout while I’m working Tuesday? I don’t want an extra garage charge hidden in the comparison.

Both properties will hold luggage after checkout. Courtyard permits the registered vehicle to remain through Tuesday afternoon under the final paid parking day, so the quoted $20 two-night parking total does not increase. Hampton also permits departure-day parking at no additional charge. In either case, confirm the vehicle at the desk that morning so it is not treated as an unregistered car after checkout.
Which one would you carry as primary for each return scenario? Keep one fallback too.

For the 9:12 p.m. Tuesday return, carry Courtyard as primary at $418.36 for the two-night base: it has the best balance among the three stops and the simpler bag pickup and airport departure. Carry Hampton as fallback at $389.18; it saves $29.18 but is less balanced for Vinings Slope. For the 7:20 a.m. Wednesday return, Courtyard remains primary at $630.20 after the added night, while Hampton remains fallback at $583.77. Hampton saves $46.43 in that scenario, but Courtyard still has the more even operating route.
Hold those two only. Nothing should be booked until the rental car is included.

Nothing has been booked. Retained primary: Courtyard Atlanta Vinings/Galleria, $418.36 complete for the two-night base, with Tuesday-night extension adding $211.84 for a $630.20 three-night total; parking is $10 nightly, and free cancellation ends February 22 at 11:59 p.m. Atlanta time, 10:59 p.m. Chicago. Retained fallback: Hampton Inn Atlanta-Cumberland Mall, $389.18 complete for two nights, with Tuesday-night extension adding $194.59 for a $583.77 three-night total; parking is included, and free cancellation ends February 21 at 11:59 p.m. Atlanta time, 10:59 p.m. Chicago. Courtyard is the lead under both return-flight scenarios. The rental car and final flight choice remain unresolved.
